title: Custom LLM-as-a-Judge Evaluator for Agent Policy
dataSources: Custom judge scores and rationales on sampled sessions, traces or spans in the Agent Stream
description: Scores agent sessions, traces or spans against the team's own policy with a custom LLM-as-a-judge evaluator in Splunk Agent Observability, and improves the judge prompt from reviewer corrections with Autotune.
value: Preset and Luna evaluators cover common risks. A custom judge scores what is specific to the business, for example whether the agent stayed within its support scope.
implementation: Add a model integration to the org, write the judge prompt, choose session, trace or span scope, and turn the evaluator on for the Agent Stream with an explicit sample rate. Correct wrong verdicts and let Autotune rewrite the prompt. An evaluator scores traces that are already stored and never blocks the reply. To stop or redirect a step inline, use Agent Control (UC-13.8.26).
visualization: Custom judge score and rationale columns in the trace or Sessions view.
knownFalsePositives: A new judge prompt is often too strict or too lenient. Treat the first weeks as calibration and correct verdicts before relying on the score.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites

A Splunk Agent Observability project for the application and one Agent Stream per environment or agent inside it. Do not create a second project for the same application: a second project splits the traces. The agent reads `SPLUNK_AO_PROJECT` and `SPLUNK_AO_AGENT_STREAM` from the environment. SaaS tenants authenticate with `SPLUNK_AO_REALM` and `SPLUNK_AO_O11Y_TOKEN`; on-prem tenants with `SPLUNK_AO_API_KEY` plus `SPLUNK_AO_CONSOLE_URL`. Install the SDK with `pip install splunk-ao` (`pip install "splunk-ao[langchain]"` for the LangChain callback).

Step 1 — Instrument the agent

The agent is already instrumented as described in UC-13.8.1: every request is a trace with at least one agent span, LLM spans carry `model`, token counts and the `tools` schemas, and tool spans carry `name`, `duration_ns` and `tool_call_id`.

Step 2 — Configure in Splunk Agent Observability

Evaluators are defined for the organization and turned on per Agent Stream, in the console (Configure Evaluators) or with `enable_evaluators`. That SDK call replaces the stream's set: anything left out is turned off. Evaluators run after the trace is stored, on a sample. A 10% rate stores every trace and scores one in ten, and a sampled trace is scored by every enabled evaluator. There is no documented default sample rate, so set it explicitly. Custom LLM-as-a-judge needs a model integration on the org; an error about a missing integration is an org setting, not agent code. On-prem can also run registered code evaluators; SaaS cannot.

Step 3 — Validate

Score a labelled set of traces from a test stream and compare the verdicts with the labels before turning it on in production. This use case was written from the Splunk Agent Observability documentation without access to a tenant, so it ships as a draft. Confirm each step in the Splunk Agent Observability console before promoting it.

Step 4 — Operationalize

Review a sample of verdicts each week, correct the wrong ones, and run Autotune. Use Experiments (UC-13.8.23) to compare prompt versions offline.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting

Missing integration error: add the model integration on the org. Verdicts drift after a model change on the integration: re-run the labelled set.
grandmaExplanation: We write our own grading rules and have a reviewer mark the assistant's answers against them.

productArtifacts.title: Custom LLM-as-a-judge evaluator
productArtifacts.body:
Where: Agent Stream > Configure Evaluators (or enable_evaluators in the SDK)
Evaluator: Custom LLM-as-a-judge (team policy)
Judge: Your prompt, run by the org's model integration
Scores: session, trace or span (choose one)
Sample rate: set explicitly for the stream; there is no documented default
Notes: Needs a model integration on the org. Autotune rewrites the prompt from reviewer corrections; it does not apply to Luna or code evaluators.
